rubric.evidence: Pre-build CDP probe (scripts/browser.mjs harness) loaded https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@huggingface/transformers@3.7.5 via the shared lib/webai.js loadPipeline({task:'image-to-text',model:'Xenova/trocr-small-handwritten',backend:'wasm',dtype:'q8'}), downloaded the canonical onnx/encoder_model_quantized.onnx + onnx/decoder_model_merged_quantized.onnx, and completed a real inference in 731 ms on an IAM handwriting line, returning [{"generated_text":"industrial, \" Mr. Brown commented, icily. \" Let us have a"}] — real decoder output, not canned. The committed route-complete validator scripts/validate-trocr-handwriting.mjs repeats real inference on every route.

pipeline('image-to-text') returns [{generated_text:string}] for a single-line handwriting crop; the page hands the model either the DrawPad bitmap (canvas.toDataURL PNG, white background + dark ink matching the IAM domain) or a CropCanvas region. Semantic sanity confirmed in the probe: coherent English transcription of a handwritten line with punctuation, exactly the IAM register the checkpoint was fine-tuned on.

worker.js pins model 'Xenova/trocr-small-handwritten', task 'image-to-text', backend wasm, dtype q8 through shared loadPipeline — no local version pin needed (trocr is supported by the shared 3.7.5 build). Readout surfaces device (WASM), token count, total ms, and tok/s after every run; models.json records runtime/transformers.js, backend/wasm, dtype/q8, sizeMB 64 (encoder 23.0 MB + decoder-merged 40.5 MB + tokenizer, verified via HF x-linked-size).

Every route mounts lib/model-loader.js createModelLoader({model:{modelId:'Xenova/trocr-small-handwritten',...}}) — the shared auto-init path: a validated cached copy initialises automatically (checking→initialising→ready); Download appears only when absent; Re-download/Update/Clear per the shared state machine. No bespoke Load button.

Shared loader renders progress with real per-file bytes via the transformersAdapter → <model-download-status> boundary; run status uses role=status aria-live=polite regions; inference failures land in the page ('Reading failed: …'), an empty pad or empty transcription is an explicit on-page state ('Write something on the pad first.' / '(no text recognised)'), and camera denial on the Wild route surfaces 'Camera unavailable: …'. Never a blank panel.

Overview: DrawPad (pointer + pen + touch, touch-action:none), Clear pad, upload dropzone (click + Enter/Space + drag-drop), two sample thumbnails (keyboard-operable role=button), crop reset, max-token range with live value, Read buttons, Copy text. Basics: pad + clear + read; manuscript crop + reset + read. Practical: dropzone/samples/crop + read-line-into-list + editable rows + copy-all + clear-list. Wild: start-camera + read-framed-writing + reticle. Multi-model: pad/photo input + language select + chained run. All are native labelled controls.

All output strings come from the worker's TextStreamer tokens and the final pipe() result; there is no canned transcription anywhere. Failure paths surface errors; '(no text recognised)' is shown only when the model genuinely returns an empty string.

Every canvas is labelled (aria-label), every button/select/range has an accessible name, statuses and outputs are polite live regions, sample thumbnails are keyboard-operable, sample elements carry descriptive alt text, and the CC-BY-SA sample gets a visible credit via public/image-credit.js. Residual: the drawing pad is inherently pointer-based bitmap input — keyboard users use the photo/sample path instead (noted on the page via the dual input design); focus styles rely on the design system + :focus-visible rules in hw.js.

Fluid flex layouts (flex:1 1 300px/240px wrap) with max-inline-size caps on canvases, 44px+ primary buttons, and the DrawPad sizes to its container; driven at 1280×800 desktop and 360×740 mobile in the committed validator and scripts/responsive-check.mjs. tap-target audit may flag small chip buttons — recorded as needs-review in models.json support per policy.

All inference runs in a module Worker (worker.js) — the main thread only draws the pad/crop overlays and appends token chips. Probe inference: 731 ms for a full line on WASM (q8, 64 MB — 3× smaller than the printed-TrOCR sibling). Streaming tokens keep the UI updating incrementally; no long main-thread loops.

guidanceConsulted.query: canvas drawing pad pointer events touch accessibility
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use semantic HTML, labelled controls, focus management, and live regions; never rely on canvas alone for meaning.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: labelled canvases, keyboard-operable thumbnails and dropzone, role=status live regions, native buttons/range/select; the bitmap pad is paired with a photo/sample path so pointer-only input is not the sole route.

openQuestions: IAM-trained recognition of heavily crossed-out or double-spaced manuscript lines is weak (visible on the Ambedkar sample) — worth an honest 'limits' callout if users misread it as a bug. The Basics page already frames clean-vs-edited lines as an experiment.
summary: TrOCR small-handwritten (Xenova ONNX, image-to-text, q8, WASM, ~64 MB, MIT) — handwriting recognition as a new family distinct from the built printed-OCR sibling (trocr-ocr): different checkpoint, different input domain (pen strokes vs print), different primary interaction (a pointer/pen drawing pad). Real probe-verified inference (731 ms, coherent IAM-register transcription), shared auto-init loader on all five routes, streaming token trace 'see inside', editable line-list digitisation workflow, live-camera reader, and a handwriting→M2M100-translation chain. Two licensed Wikimedia Commons samples (CC BY-SA 4.0 exercise-book note with visible credit; public-domain Ambedkar manuscript), EXIF stripped, registered in the provenance ledger.
